observation.visible_scene: A sunlit alpine ski slope with a chairlift support tower (orange-padded base) on the left, snow-covered peaks in the background, a bright low sun producing a starburst and lens flare, and a thin marker pole with a small red flag on the open slope. A lone skier is on the foreground run-out, and the lift carries empty chairs along its cable.
visible_changes: A skier moves diagonally from near the tower base toward the lower-right of the frame, growing slightly larger as they approach the camera, and exits through the bottom edge around the mid-to-late part of the excerpt; after that the foreground slope is empty of skiers.
A second skier, briefly visible at the bottom-right corner in the first two frames, moves right and leaves the frame almost immediately.

The chairlift chairs travel steadily along the cable: the prominent right-hand chair shifts toward the upper-right (toward the sun) and the left-hand chairs drift toward the upper-left, consistent with continuous lift motion rather than a single pose.

The camera gradually tightens (zoom/dolly-in) on the tower and backdrop: the tower crossbar rises higher in frame, the orange base pad and chairs grow larger, and the sun's flare intensifies, so apparent chair/skier displacement is partly camera-driven.
The bright sun, lens flare, snow texture, mountains, marker pole, and tower remain persistent throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The skier's origin before the crop and destination after exiting the bottom edge are unseen.
Whether the lift is running loaded or empty uphill/downhill and the full cycle of chair positions beyond this segment are not established.
The cause of the camera tightening (zoom vs. forward movement) cannot be determined from the frames alone.
uncertain_details: Exact direction of chair travel along each cable line is ambiguous due to simultaneous zoom and glare.
Whether the right-edge figure in frame 1–2 is a separate skier or a transient artifact of cropping is not fully certain.
The skier's speed and technique (turning vs. straight glide) are hard to resolve at this resolution.
